drafts.title: Choosing Between VLLM and llama.cpp for Gemma3:27b & Qwen3 32B on Multi-GPU AMD Setup?
drafts.body:
I came across a 2025 Reddit post where a user with two RX 7900 XTXs and one RX 7800 XT (about 64GB total VRAM) tested inference speed on Gemma3:27b and Qwen3 32B using VLLM and llama.cpp backends. Their data is a bit dated and specific to their setup, but it hints at notable speed differences between these backends on AMD hardware.

Given that performance can vary widely with model size, GPU architecture, and backend optimizations, has anyone recently compared VLLM and llama.cpp on similar AMD multi-GPU rigs? Specifically, which backend tends to handle these large models faster or more efficiently? Any insights on how VRAM distribution across these cards influences the choice would be helpful.

drafts.title: Inference Speed Tradeoffs for Gemma3:27b and Qwen3 32B on AMD GPUs: VLLM vs llama.cpp?
drafts.body:
A Reddit user from mid-2025 shared their experience running Gemma3:27b and Qwen3 32B on a multi-GPU AMD setup (two RX 7900 XTXs plus one RX 7800 XT). They compared inference speeds between VLLM and llama.cpp but the results are somewhat dated and tied to their exact hardware.

For those with similar AMD GPU configurations totaling around 64GB VRAM, does anyone observe a consistent speed advantage with either backend when running these large models? Also, how critical is backend selection versus other factors like quantization or model loading strategies? Understanding these tradeoffs could help clarify which setup is more practical for heavy inference tasks.
